'''William''' "'''Chuck'''" '''Easttom II''' (born October 5, 1968) is an American scientist working in [[computer science]], [[cyber security]], [[cryptography]], [[digital forensics]], [[quantum computing]], [[aerospace engineering]], [[artificial intelligence]], [[machine learning]], and [[systems engineering]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=William (Chuck) Easttom II {{!}} Pearson IT Certification |url=https://www.pearsonitcertification.com/authors/bio/3865ac48-d2ea-4ef9-ae5d-88c8b7a0cbb0 |access-date=2024-02-16 |website=www.pearsonitcertification.com}}</ref>

== Education ==
Easttom holds a B.A. from [[Southeastern Oklahoma State University]], a M.Ed. from [[Southeastern Oklahoma State University]], a master's degree in Applied Computer Science from [[Northcentral University]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://alumnius.net/northcentral_univers-11143-year-2011#alumni|title=Northcentral University Alumni}}</ref> and a master's degree in Systems Engineering from the [[University of Texas at El Paso]], a master's degree in Defense and Strategic Studies from [[University of Texas at El Paso]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://hackerhalted.com/speakers/|title=Speaker Bio|date=8 July 2020 }}</ref> as well as a D.Sc. [[Doctor of Science]] in cyber security from [[Capitol Technology University]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://events.secureworldexpo.com/speakers/chuck-easttom/|title=Secure World Speaker Bio}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://saiconference.com/FICC2019/Speakers|title=Keynote Speakers Bio}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.captechu.edu/blog/easttom-cyber-war-malware-weapon-of-choice|title=Easttom: in cyber war, malware is "the weapon of choice"}}</ref> dissertation topic "A Comparative Study Of Lattice Based Algorithms For Post Quantum Computing", a [[Doctor of Philosophy]] in Technology focused on Nanotechnology<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://gufaculty360.georgetown.edu/s/contact/0031Q00002CafP5QAJ/william-easttom|title=Faculty Bio}}</ref> dissertation topic "The Effects of Complexity on Carbon Nanotube Failures", and a Ph.D.[[Doctor of Philosophy]] in Computer Science from [[University of Portsmouth]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.amazon.com/Chuck-Easttom/e/B001IYZ6I8%3Fref=dbs_a_mng_rwt_scns_share| website=Amazon | title=Chuck Easttom }}</ref> dissertation topic "A Systematic Framework for Network Forensics Using Graph Theory".

== Professional work ==
In addition to computer security, Easttom has done work in [[software engineering]],<ref>{{Cite web| url =https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=l-S2ooZMgrY|title= EC Council CASE Java|website= [[YouTube]]|date= November 2018}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web| url =http://cedat.mak.ac.ug/wp-content/themes/CEDAT-Theme/curriculums/bsc-electrical-engineering/CMP-1201.pdf|title= Computer Programming Course Syllabus}}</ref> [[applied mathematics]], [[aerospace engineering]], [[quantum computing]], [[artificial intelligence]], [[machine learning]],<ref>{{Cite web|url =https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/abstract/document/9031266|title=A comparative study of machine learning algorithms for use in breast cancer studies}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url =https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/abstract/document/9720819|title=Easttom, C., Alsmadi, I (2022). A Comparative Study of Machine Learning Algorithms for Identifying Mental States from EEG Recordings}}</ref> and other areas. He has authored 44 books<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.technosecurity.us/tx/speakers/chuck-easttom|title=Speaker Bio}}{{Dead link|date=July 2020 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> on computer security, programming languages, [[Linux]], cyber forensics, [[quantum computing]], [[computer networks]], penetration testing, and [[cryptography]]. His books are used as textbooks for both undergraduate and graduate programs at over 60 universities.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.liberty.edu/online/wp-content/uploads/CSCI511_CourseGuide.pdf| title=CS 511 digital forensics.}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://pages.southwesterncc.edu/kirks/bookorder.htm| title=CCT 121 Computer Crime Investigation.}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.tamuct.edu/syllabi/docs/2017_Fall/20170880042.pdf| title=CIS 4345, CRN 80042, Network and Systems Security}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.cs.fsu.edu/~langley/CIS4385-2018-1/Syllabus.html| title=CIS 4385 Cybercrime Detection and Digital Forensics}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://cfrs.gmu.edu/assets/Summer15/TCOM-CFRS-661-001-Summer2015-Syllabus-v1.pdf| title=TCOM/CFRS 661 Digital Media Forensics}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://cse.sc.edu/~farkas/csce201-2015/csce201-syllabus.htm| title=CSCE 201 Introduction to Computer Security}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://ksuweb.kennesaw.edu/~ashaw8/acst3530-01-Summer16/acst3530s1syllabus.html| title=ACST 3530 - Linux Operating Systems and Networking}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.personal.kent.edu/~jbolen/comt36330/comt_36330.htm|title=COMT 36330 LAN Security Fundamentals}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.citadel.edu/root/mathcs-courses/descriptions/undergraduate-computerscience/58-academics/schools/ssm/mathematics-and-computer-science/22597-csci-227-cybersecurity-non-cs|title=CSCI: Principles and Practices of Cybersecurity }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.apus.edu/z/course-syllabus/ISSC630.pdf|title=ISSC630: Advanced Cybercrime Analysis }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://itech.fgcu.edu/faculty/zalewski/CNT4104/CNT4104-3.html|title=CNT 4104 Software Project in Computer Networks }}</ref> He is an inventor with 27 patented computer science inventions.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://patft.uspto.gov/netacgi/nph-Parser?Sect1=PTO2&Sect2=HITOFF&p=1&u=%2Fnetahtml%2FPTO%2Fsearch-bool.html&r=0&f=S&l=50&TERM1=easttom&FIELD1=INNM&co1=AND&TERM2=&FIELD2=&d=PTXT|title=United States Patent Office }}</ref> He is a frequent speaker at  major cybersecurity conferences.<ref>{{Cite web| url =https://www.hackerhalted.com/hacker-halted-2019/agenda/|title= Hacker Halted|date= 2017-01-18}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web| url =https://events.secureworldexpo.com/agenda/dallas-tx-2018/|title= Secure World}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web| url =https://www.eventscribe.com/2018/ISC2/agenda.asp?pfp=agenda|title= ISC2 Security Congress}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web| url =https://www.defcon.org/html/defcon-25/dc-25-workshops.html|title= DEFCON}}</ref>

Easttom was part of the team that created the original  [[CompTIA]] Security+ <ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.slideshare.net/jmailen/comptia-sme-announcement-sept-2002|title=CompTIA Security+ SME List|date=2016-02-09}}</ref> and  [[CompTIA]] Linux+ exams. He created the OSFCE (OSForensics Certified Examiner) course and test,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.osforensics.com/training.html|title=OSForensics Training}}</ref> the EC Council Certified Encryption Specialist course and certification test,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZLuz60ImHuM|title=ECES|website=[[YouTube]] |date=3 July 2017 }}</ref> and EC Council CAST Advanced Encryption course <ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.jblearning.com/catalog/9781284121841/5|title=Author Bio}}{{Dead link|date=July 2020 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> as well as working on other  [[EC-Council]] certifications <ref>{{Cite web|url=https://iclass.eccouncil.org/schedule/certified-application-security-engineer-live-february-18-20-washington-dc/|title=EC Council Certified Application Security Engineer|access-date=20 November 2018}}</ref>

Easttom has been involved in numerous IEEE standards. He is currently the Chair of  IEEE P3123 - Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning (AI/ML) Terminology and Data Formats Working Group,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://sagroups.ieee.org/3123/|title=IEEE P3123}}</ref> a member of IEEE 2731 BCI unified terminology working group,<ref>{{Cite journal|title=IEEE 2731|year=2021 |doi=10.1109/OJEMB.2021.3057471  |doi-access=free|pmid=35402984 |last1=Easttom |first1=C. |last2=Bianchi |first2=L. |last3=Valeriani |first3=D. |last4=Nam |first4=C. S. |last5=Hossaini |first5=A. |last6=Zapala |first6=D. |last7=Roman-Gonzalez |first7=A. |last8=Singh |first8=A. K. |last9=Antonietti |first9=A. |last10=Sahonero-Alvarez |first10=G. |last11=Balachandran |first11=P. |journal=IEEE Open Journal of Engineering in Medicine and Biology |volume=2 |pages=91–96 |pmc=8901026 }}</ref> a former member (2017 to 2019) of  IEEE Software & Systems Engineering Standards Committee. Working on the DevOps 2675,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pearsonitcertification.com/authors/bio/8c7754c9-7309-40b5-90f8-70e7cc5ac318|title=Pearson Bio}}</ref> a member of IEEE P2995 - Trial-Use Standard for a Quantum Algorithm Design and Development Standards Group,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://sagroups.ieee.org/quadd|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220224081928/https://sagroups.ieee.org/quadd/|url-status=dead|archive-date=February 24, 2022|title=IEEE P2995}}</ref> and Vice Chair IEEE P23026 - Systems and Software Engineering—Engineering and Management of Websites for Systems, Software, and Services Information<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://standards.ieee.org/ieee/23026/10425/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220223220018/https://standards.ieee.org/ieee/23026/10425/|url-status=dead|archive-date=February 23, 2022|title=IEEE P23026}}</ref>

web|url=http://www.smartplanet.com/blog/bulletin/nsa-proof-products-protective-or-a-profit-motive/| title=NSA proof products: protective or a profit motive?}}</ref> and other media outlets,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.bankinfosecurity.com/interviews/what-jpmorgan-chase-breach-teaches-us-i-2982| title=What the JPMorgan Chase Breach Teaches Us}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www2.ljworld.com/news/2006/aug/06/hackers_infiltrate_web_site/| title=Hackers infiltrate Web site}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.forensicfocus.com/News/article/sid=2902/| [[Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers|IEEE]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Chuck Easttom &#124; IEEE Computer Society |date=16 January 2020 |url=https://www.computer.org/profiles/Chuck-Easttom |access-date=2020-11-09 |language=en-US}}</ref> He is also a Senior member of the IEEE <ref>{{Cite web| url =http://interface.computer.org/ieee-computer-society-new-class-of-senior-members/|title= IEEE Senior Member|date= 2019-05-06}}</ref>  and Senior member of the ACM.<ref>{{Cite web| url =https://awards.acm.org/award_winners/easttom_0447967|title= ACM Senior Member}}</ref> He is also a member of the  American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics (AIAA).

Easttom was Editor in Chief for the ''American Journal of Science and Engineering'' from 2018 to 2022.<ref>{{Cite web| url =http://ajse.us/editorial-board/|title= American Journal of Science and Engineering}}</ref> He was also the director of the Quantum Computing and Cryptography Lab at Capitol Technology University,<ref>{{Cite web| url =https://www.captechu.edu/student-experience/labs-and-centers/quantum-computing-and-cryptography-research-lab|title= Quantum Computing and Cryptography Research Lab}}</ref> from 2019 to 2022 he was an adjunct professor for the University of Dallas,<ref>{{Cite web| url =https://udallas.edu/cob/about/adjunct-faculty/easttom_chuck.php|title= University of Dallas Faculty Page}}</ref> he is currently an adjunct lecturer for Georgetown University <ref>{{Cite web| url =https://gufaculty360.georgetown.edu/s/contact/0031Q00002CafP5QAJ/william-easttom|title= Georgetown Faculty Page}}</ref> and an adjunct professor for Vanderbilt University.<ref>{{cite book| chapter-url=https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-031-12304-7_3| chapter= Basic Information Theory| year= 2022| pages= 51–73| publisher= Springer| doi= 10.1007/978-3-031-12304-7_3| isbn= 9783031123047| last1= Easttom| first1= Chuck| title= Modern Cryptography}}</ref>

Chuck Easttom lives in Plano Texas <ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.jissec.org/Contents/V13/N3/V13N3-Easttom.html.}}</ref> with his wife Teresa.

== Books ==

Easttom has authored 44 computer science books.  These include:
* ''Beginning JavaScript, 1st Edition''.WordWare Publishing (2001)
* ''JBuilder 7.0 EJB Programming''.WordWare Publishing (2002)
* ''Programming Fundamentals in C++''.Charles River Learning. 1st Edition, Charles River Media (2003)
* ''Essential Linux Administration: A Comprehensive Guide for Beginners''. Cengage Press (2011)
* ''System Forensics, Investigation, and Response, 2nd Edition'', Jones & Bartlett (2013) <!-- No ISBN number, ASIN instead :https://www.amazon.com/Forensics-Investigation-Response-Easttom-Paperback/dp/B00OVNM2G2 -->
** ''System Forensics, Investigation, and Response (Information Systems Security & Assurance), 3rd Edition'' Jones and Bartlett (2017) {{ISBN|978-1284121841}}
* ''Certified Cyber Forensics Professional All in One Guide''. McGraw-Hill (2014) {{ISBN|978-0071839761}}
* ''Computer Security Fundamentals (3rd Edition)''.  Pearson IT Cybersecurity Curriculum (ITCC) (2016) {{ISBN|978-0789757463}}
* ''CompTIA Security+ Study Guide: Exam SY0-501''. John Wiley & Sons (2017)
* ''Penetration Testing Fundamentals: A Hands-On Guide to Reliable Security Audits (1st Edition).''  Pearson IT Cybersecurity Curriculum (2018) {{ISBN|978-0789759375}}
* ''CompTIA Security+ Practice Tests: Exam SY0-501''.  Sybex (2018)
* ''Network Defense and Countermeasures: Principles and Practices, 3rd Edition''  Pearson IT Cybersecurity Curriculum (ITCC)) (2018)
* ''Networking Fundamentals, 3rd Edition.''  Goodheart-Wilcox Publishing) (2018)
